transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendez (Aegis Head of ML), Rina Patel (Aegis CTO), Samir Gupta (Aegis Infra), Mei Wong (Aegis Privacy)

Auto-summary: Aegis Tech is looking to move from OpenAI due to cost and data residency; exploring Redwood Dedicated and Private options; wants compatibility with existing evals and toolchain (vLLM/TGI used in-house); security gating (SOC2, KMS, SSO) required before procurement.

00:00 Jordan Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intros, i'm jordan from redwood, and with me priya our solutions engineer and lena on cs.
00:08 Carlos Mendez: hey all carlos here, quick note we got the calendar invite, excited to run through migration options.
00:12 Rina Patel: rina here, CTO. we're on a tight timeline Q4 for pilot, ideally within 4 weeks.
00:18 Priya Shah: great, our goal today to understand your current stack and blockers, then outline dedicated sizing and what a pilot looks like.
00:26 Samir Gupta: ran the infra side for aegis, we run most stuff in GCP; currently everything hitting OpenAI via API keys, we've also been experimenting with vLLM on prem for cost reasons.
00:36 Jordan Kim: cool can you run through volume? tokens per month, sequence lengths, typical concurrency?
00:43 Carlos Mendez: rough numbers, right now avg 25M tokens/month, spikes to 5k concurrent short-chat requests during peak, seq lengths mostly 512-1024 for context. cost is creeping up 30% qtr over qtr.
00:56 Priya Shah: that helps. two big decision points we usually see: parity with your evals (we've found small model behavior can shift) and operational constraints like VPC/KMS/SSO. how strict is your data residency and audit requirement?
01:08 Mei Wong: fairly strict — we need SOC 2 Type II, audit logs retained for 1 year, and customer data encrypted with our KMS; ideally no plaintext stored outside our VPC.
01:18 Rina Patel: also must verify that moving off openai doesn't cause performance regressions on our rerank/eval suite. we use a mix of larger instruct models and a couple of fine-tuned variants.
01:28 Priya Shah: on compatibility, Redwood Dedicated can expose a compatible API surface but there are some differences in streaming and function calling semantics depending on model variant. we do a parity pass during onboarding and can run your evals against our curated model catalog.
01:44 Carlos Mendez: ok important: we use vLLM and TGI for internal workloads. will those map to Redwood runtime? any gotchas with kv cache or quantized checkpoints?
01:56 Priya Shah: good question. our runtime supports many open formats; for vLLM/TGI checkpoints we often do a quick verify. kv cache handling and continuous attention implementations can differ, so we'll validate with your baseline prompts. some tokenization edge cases pop up in transcriptions — like special tokens in your fine-tunes.
02:16 Samir Gupta: what about autoscaling and bursting? our traffic is spiky and we want predictable latency SLOs.
02:22 Jordan Kim: Dedicated has reserved pools plus burst capacity into shared hosted for overflow. you can configure autoscale thresholds and we have fallback policies to reduce latency impact.
02:34 Rina Patel: and cost — can you ballpark cost vs openai?
02:38 Jordan Kim: ballpark, customers often see 20-50% cost reduction depending on throughput and batching. critical is caching and batch tuning — we can recommend quantization profiles to drop GPU footprint. we'll send a pricing sheet post-call.
02:50 Priya Shah: also note some optimizations in our runtime (attention kernels, fused ops) give better p99 latency especially on long context.
03:01 Carlos Mendez: about eval parity: we run automated evals for hallucination and factuality. will we be able to run the same eval harness against Redwood to compare exact metrics?
03:12 Priya Shah: yes, we'll run your evals in a side-by-side benchmark. we usually do a three-way: OpenAI baseline, Redwood Hosted, and Redwood Dedicated. if you have vLLM/TGI artifacts we'll add those too.
03:27 Rina Patel: any differences in response formats? we rely on function calling and structured json.
03:33 Priya Shah: function calling is supported but slightly different naming in the rpc. we can map the names or add a shim. streaming can be chunked differently, but we preserve ordering. we'll document the exact deltas.
03:47 Mei Wong: security specifics: KMS integration, HSM? SSO/saml? audit logs?
03:53 Jordan Kim: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and HSM options for key material. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, we have RBAC, and audit logs with configurable retention. we'll share SOC2 and penetration test reports.
04:07 Samir Gupta: network, can we do VPC peering or private link? we don't want any public egress for inference traffic.
04:13 Priya Shah: for Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private connectivity, and for Private deployments we can deploy into your VPC/on-prem cluster. some customers use a tunnel to the control plane but keep data plane in their network.
04:26 Carlos Mendez: are there known gotchas migrating fine-tunes? we have a few proprietary fine-tuned models.
04:31 Priya Shah: fine-tune migration depends on format; we can import weights if they're in supported formats. if it's OpenAI style fine-tunes, sometimes we reprovision as a serving variant or convert to a quantized checkpoint. we'll need to test for behavior changes.
04:45 Rina Patel: about the pilot, we want to run a POC with 1-2 models, run 100k evals, and compare latency/throughput/cost and quality. can that be done in 2-4 weeks?
04:56 Jordan Kim: yes typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. deliverables: benchmark report, parity notes, recommended production config.
05:04 Carlos Mendez: ok to have priya run an initial benchmark with our eval harness?
05:09 Priya Shah: absolutely, please share the harness and sample data. we'll run a replicated test and share results. link to benchmark spreadsheet: [redwood_benchmarks_v2.xlsx] (we'll upload to your workspace).
05:24 Samir Gupta: curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated pool is saturated will requests drop or failover to hosted?
05:30 Jordan Kim: we configure fallbacks — either queue, reject with backpressure, or route to compatible hosted models. customers choose policy per route.
05:41 Rina Patel: procurement/legal: what are typical contract terms for Dedicated? SLA, data residency clauses?
05:47 Jordan Kim: we do reserved capacity contracts with SLAs for uptime and latency, can include data residency and increased audit clauses for enterprise deals. legal will follow after the pilot.
05:58 Mei Wong: one last question: does Redwood's runtime match openai tokenization exactly? we saw small diffs that impacted reranker scores.
06:06 Priya Shah: tokenization is model dependent and sometimes differs slightly. we can run tokenization diffs as part of the parity checks and patch via tokenizer config.
06:18 Jordan Kim: ok i'll recap next steps: i'll send pricing and dedicated configs; priya will share benchmark templates and run evals; lena will coordinate pilot onboarding; rina to confirm stakeholders.
06:31 Rina Patel: sounds good, we'll confirm scope by friday. thanks everyone.
06:35 Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for technical deep dive.
06:38 [call ends]

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., "kv cash" instead of KV cache in one portion). Some speaker labels may collapse in the automated export.
